correctness.rationale: Proved spider laws: all peripheral b_i jobs match private d_i or a_i; the center fails under job-side vertex order iff processed last and each arm job chooses a_i, giving 1/((m+1)2^m). Under uniformly random edge priorities it fails iff each arm internal edge a_i b_i is earliest of the three arm edges, giving 3^-m independently across arms. Thus the two-point stochastic order flips precisely for m>=4; the m=4 gap is 1/6480, with E[M_V]=399/80 and E[M_E]=404/81. For sharp n<=13 cutoff, independently enumerated all free trees with a second generator and both bipartition orientations and evaluated a separate exact Fraction first-edge/first-job recurrence: a single positive orientation at n=13, none for n<=12. Inspected pinned verify.py, including its independent induction-complete leaf-extension tree generator and canonical centers. This is exhaustive finite calculation, not a proof of an all-order tree classification.

evidence: General randomized greedy matching and average labeled-tree analysis do not provide per-oriented-tree inequalities through n=12
